subject: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Martin <clare@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment

Clare — quick note from our side. Over the last 18 hours we've observed a steady decline (roughly 22% aggregate) in effective reserved throughput for your Dedicated GPU pool backing the inference endpoints tied to FC-order-service. The immediate impact shows as increased request queueing and a small rise in 500/502 errors during peak windows (see attached trace + summary).

We believe the immediate contributors are:
- A spike in long-context inference jobs from one of your new features that triggers heavier KV cache churn.
- A gradual reduction of available headroom due to co-located burst workloads that saturated pooling heuristics during autoscale evaluations.

Mitigation options we can take in the next 30–120 minutes (recommendation in bold):
- Temporary routing of a % of traffic to an isolated backup model (lower-cost variant) to relieve queueing while preserving correctness for low-risk routes. (Recommended: 20% of non-critical endpoints)
- Force an emergency increase in reserved slices for your Dedicated pool for the next 3 hours (if you authorize a short burst commit).
- Apply a dynamic prefix KV cache pin (engineering) to reduce warm-start overhead for long-context sessions (30–45m work, then flips).
- Short-term soft-limits to cap per-tenant concurrency for the offending feature (will throttle some user requests; opt-in by you).

Action requested: please confirm which of the above you'd like us to execute. If helpful, we can stand up a 15-min executive sync at 09:00 PT to walk through tradeoffs.

Jonas
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Clare Martin <clare@fastcommerce.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@fastcommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:01:23 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment

Thanks Jonas — this is alarming, thanks for the quick flag. A few clarifying Qs:
- How long will the error-rate uplift persist if we do nothing?
- What is the customer-visible latency delta if you route 20% of traffic to the lower-cost variant? We can tolerate 50–100ms extra for background jobs but not checkout flows.
- If we authorize a short burst commit, what's the minimum billing/commit increment? ProcureOps wants the expected delta.

We want to avoid throttling the checkout path. Please mark which endpoints are critical vs background on your routing plan.

-Clare
Head of Platform, FastCommerce

On Sun, Sep 13, 2026 at 08:45 Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa / Vivek — raising for ops attention. Full traces attached. The immediate window is fragile through the US afternoon.
>
> On the recommended path: I think we should 1) pin KV for the largest long-context keyspace, 2) route non-checkout traffic to the cheaper variant, and 3) queue an engineering hotfix to avoid autoscale misclassification. Tessa, can you get infra to prioritize the pin?
>
> Jonas
>
---

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:02:14 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment

On it — infra will stand up the KV pin and a temporary routing policy within 25–40 minutes. I'll keep checkout endpoints exempt by default; need the endpoint list from Clare to map exact route IDs. Also: if Clare approves, we can do a 3-hour 10% burst; procurement details inlined below (ballpark):
- Minimum burst increment: $4.8k (3 hours at current reserved rate)
- Auto-revert to previous allocation at end of window

I'll push the runbook link to you in the next update.

Tessa
Sr. Infra PM

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Martin <clare@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 13:24:53 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment

Clare — thanks for the quick turn. Answers inline: 
- If no mitigation is applied we expect elevated queueing/errors to continue for the remainder of the US business day with a slowly improving tail overnight; estimated increased error budget ~0.8–1.5% for high-volume routes (checkout exempt).
- Routing 20% non-critical traffic to the lower-cost variant: median latency delta +85ms, p95 +220ms for those requests. We'll scope routing so checkout/confirm endpoints are not part of that 20%.
- Burst commit: Tessa's estimate is correct — $4.8k for a 3-hour 10% reserved slice (we can scale up the delta if you want larger headroom). Procurement note: we can invoice as an overage credit against the monthly commitment or as a separate short-term addendum.

Proposed immediate plan (execute upon Clare approval):
1) Execute KV pin (T+25m) — reduces warmup churn for long contexts.
2) Route background/reporting endpoints to the lower-cost variant at 20% (T+30m).
3) Apply 3-hour 10% burst on request from FastCommerce (billing as temporary commit); will auto-revert.
4) Engineering to follow up with autoscale classifier fix (ETA 2 business days).

If you approve, I'll brief our execs and yours on the customer impact and proposed credits. We should also schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow to firm up the longer-term changes (quantization profiles, model partitioning and persistent KV strategies).

Jonas

---

From: Clare Martin <clare@fastcommerce.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@fastcommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 16:42:18 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved throughput attrition — urgent mitigation & exec alignment

Jonas / team — please proceed with 1) KV pin and 2) routing background endpoints (we'll provide route IDs in the next 10 minutes). We approve the temporary 3-hour 10% burst commit — ProcureOps is copied; please send the short addendum for signature and we will expedite.

We also request an executive note outlining the incident impact and a proposal for credits to cover customer refunds if any checkout latency breaches occur. I'll need it before EOD our time.

-Clare
